description: The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in ISO 8601 time interval format. In the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL. Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945". Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. Identifying the hydropower scheme type is crucial for understanding the research contribution related to energy generation methods, environmental impact, efficiency, and technological innovation in hydropower development.

label: emission color

For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" whose titleEIDR is "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J" has several edits, e.g. "10.5240/1F2A-E1C5-680A-14C6-E76B-I" and "10.5240/8A35-3BEE-6497-5D12-9E4F-3". Since schema.org types like Movie and TVEpisode can be used for both works and their multiple expressions, it is possible to use titleEIDR alone (for a general description), or alongside editEIDR for a more edit-specific description.

label: individual light history

label: integration with editors

label: drawn from

label: duration of programme

label: genetic algorithm technique

label: geographical dataset

label: geometric correction
description: Geometric correction (sometimes abbreviated to geocorrection) is the process of transforming the X and Y dimensions of a remotely sensed image, so that spatial distortions in the original image are eliminated or minimised and the output X and Y dimensions correspond to a chosen geographic reference system.

label: geometry specification
description: Geometry specification represents the specific geometric parameters, such as shape, dimensions, and features, that are defined and utilized in the research study to characterize the interfacial properties and mechanical behavior of a functionally graded material produced via selective laser melting.

label: grounded theory
description: Qualitative method that enables to study a particular phenomenon or process and discover new theories that are based on the collection and analysis of real world data.

label: habitat

label: hallucination type

label: monitoring duration

label: controlled experiment
description: A Controlled Experiment is a scientific study where one or more variables are manipulated while others are kept constant to determine the effect of the manipulated variables. It involves the use of control groups and experimental groups to establish causal relationships and validate hypotheses. This property indicates that the research contribution includes empirical evidence obtained through such rigorously designed experiments.

label: models (estimators)
description: Model (estimator, mathematical function) used to model dependent variable as a function of independent variable(s)

label: model vs. observations
description: Defines wether modeled (predicted) values are visually compared in dependence of observed values on the graph (usually called 'scatter graph', with observed values on x-axis and predicted values on y-axis), or some characteristics related to the comparison

label: mobility
description: Describes the mobility of the charge (either electron or hole), its value, and the method used to obtain the information.

label: missing time period
description: Period where AIS data are missing

label: multi-fidelity
description: Judge configurations on multiple budgets to discard unsuitable configurations early on. This will result in a massive speed-up, depending on the budgets.

label: neural network developed
description: Neural network developed in research

label: neighbor feature
description: Refer to incorporation of neighborhood information by means of contextual words or distance

label: context efficiency
description: Context Efficiency refers to the effectiveness with which external tool outputs are incorporated into the LLM’s context window while minimizing unnecessary token consumption and redundancy. It evaluates how well the system optimizes context usage to maintain performance and reduce computational cost. In research, this property emphasizes innovations in context management, prompt optimization, or techniques that improve the balance between information richness and efficiency.

label: context extension method
description: The technique used during training or mid-training to extend a model’s supported context length, such as continued pre-training with longer sequences or positional-encoding methods like RoPE scaling.

label: multivariate frequency analysis
description: Define method used for multivariate frequency analysis, or wether multivariate or univariate frequency analysis was used, frequency analysis means probabilistic analysis of duration, return period (frequency) and intensities (magnitude) of phenomena, such us, water level, river flow, earthquake, rainfall, etc.

label: continent
description: continent of which the subject is a part

description: This field indicates the number of attention heads in the multi-head attention mechanism. Each attention head can focus on different parts of the input sequence, allowing the model to capture various aspects of the data simultaneously

description: Conditions under which the experiments were run; like temperature, pressure, rpm etc.

description: The specific model or models of open access (e.g. apc based open access, green open access) under investigation

The adjective "deep" in deep learning refers to the use of multiple layers in the network. Methods used can be either supervised, semi-supervised or unsupervised.

description: lineage refers to a direct or indirect genealogical descent or origin of a particular research concept, methodology, or idea. It highlights the historical development or evolution of a specific aspect within the research domain.

label: living/updatable
description: Ability of the tool to update the screened references by automatically including recent and relevant articles.

label: literature search method
description: The 'literature search method' predicate describes the systematic approach or techniques employed by researchers to identify, select, and review relevant academic and scientific literature related to their study. This includes databases searched, keywords used, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and any tools or protocols followed to ensure a comprehensive and unbiased collection of prior work.

label: logic type
description: The logic type that is considered by the Symbolic AI model (e.g., Informal logic, Formal logic, Symbolic logic, Mathematical logic)

label: dictionaries evaluated

label: dietary assessment method
description: The method used to evaluate and quantify the dietary intake of individuals, often involving the assessment of macro and micro nutrients consumed by the subjects.

label: department metadata
description: Refers to the department of authors that have published the thesis

label: knowledge cutoff date
description: In the context of large language models (LLMs), the "knowledge cutoff date" refers to the latest point in time when the data used for pretraining the model was collected. This property defines the temporal scope of the model's knowledge, indicating that the model may not be aware of events, developments, or information that occurred after this date. It is crucial for understanding the model's limitations in providing up-to-date insights.

label: math format
description: Mathematical Representation Formats

label: creation type

label: credit text
description: Text that can be used to credit person(s) and/or organization(s) associated with a published Creative Work.

label: maximum number of parameters (in million)

label: culture conditions

label: meta-analysis

It is used to provide a comprehensive and quantitative summary of existing research findings, enhancing the reliability and generalizability of results.

label: created web application

label: measurement value

label: data assimilation technique

This technique is crucial in fields such as meteorology, oceanography, and environmental science, where it helps to combine real-world measurements with model simulations to produce more reliable and precise results. Describing this property in a research paper highlights the specific approach or algorithm employed to assimilate data, which can be a significant contribution to advancing modeling and forecasting methodologies.

label: data cleaning
description: Data Cleaning means to remove duplications, missing values, false information, etc. to make data ready to be used.

label: luminous used

label: dashboard developer country
description: The country where the research or development of the dashboard is based in or originated from.

label: material accessible
description: Material Accessible refers to whether the research materials, such as datasets, software, experimental protocols, or other resources used or produced in the research, are made available and accessible to other researchers or the public. This property indicates the openness and reproducibility of the research by enabling others to access and utilize the materials for verification, replication, or further study.

label: mass loading
description: Mass loading is defined by the weight of electrode slurry on the current collector in a unit area.

label: mapping to other identifiers
description: Describes the linking with other identifiers within different infrastructures

label: manually attaching full-text

label: maintenance
description: Lists if entity was actively maintained in 2022

label: number of accepted submissions
description: Number of submission accepted to an event (e.g., scientific event) or a journal

label: threat to validity
description: Risk that may affect the validity of an empirical study.

label: internal validity
description: Internal validity is the extent to which you can be confident that a cause-and-effect relationship established in a study cannot be explained by other factors.

label: external validity
description: External validity is the validity of applying the conclusions of a scientific study outside the context of that study.

label: construct validity
description: Construct validity concerns the extent to which your test or measure accurately assesses what it's supposed to.

label: conclusion validity
description: Conclusion validity is the degree to which conclusions we reach about relationships in our data are reasonable.

label: benchmark result

label: accuracy
